metadata.lot_semantics: The land lot on which the Goodman Texaco Centre stands, named by the 2025 Considerate Contractors list as the site of Goodman's Project Galaxy conversion works. It is a land-grant lot section, not a building footprint, data-hall extent or current work extent.
metadata.building_layer_crosscheck: Lands Department building layer via CSDI (landsd_rcd_1637211194312_35158, FeatureServer 0), point-intersect query at HK1980 830403 E, 825021 N (tmp/research-round43-apac/r43-apac-hk-building-at-als-point.json, sha256 430ac402631a7a5458e1effb04b5aff931b68f78e1c22947ba53616c42ecdca6): one feature, BuildingCSUID '3040325021T20050430' (identical to the ALS GeoAddress), BuildingNameEN 'Goodman Texaco Centre', BuildingNameTC '嘉民德高中心', Status 'Active'. 99.6% of its 3,054 m2 footprint lies inside Lot 472 S.A, and it covers 99.9% of the lot. The building and the lot therefore coincide; the footprint is a cross-check only and is not selected. The round42 name query '%TEXACO%' returned nothing because the stored name is mixed-case.

metadata.identity_bridge: The Considerate Contractors list (evidence ap43-hkg10-ccsas-texaco-centre-lot) gives 'Section A of Lot No. 472 in D.D. 443' as the Goodman Texaco Centre lot; this record and code table resolve that legal description to LotCSUID '463000472    A'.

semantics.precision_scope: Every native vertex of D.D. 443 Lot 472 S.A is transformed once with the recorded PROJ operation and rounded to seven decimals. The lot is the government-recorded land of the Goodman Texaco Centre, whose conversion is HKG10; it is a land-grant lot section, not a building footprint, data-hall extent or current work extent. The government address point for Goodman Texaco Centre and Goodman's own listing point both fall inside it and are not selected. The display anchor is the planar shoelace centroid of the transformed ring in source vertex order, verified inside it.
semantics.horizontal_uncertainty_unknown_reason: The lot layer states no positional tolerance for this boundary; the datum-operation accuracy is not a boundary accuracy.
